title: A review of Bundibugyo virus and the 2026 outbreak: lessons for epidemic preparedness.
abstract: The ongoing 2026 outbreak of Ebola virus disease caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda has renewed attention to one of the least studied human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses. Since its discovery in western Uganda in 2007, only two recognised outbreaks of BDBV had been reported, limiting opportunities to define the epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, clinical spectrum, and optimal management of BDBV or to develop species-specific countermeasures. The current outbreak, declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern by WHO on May 17, 2026, has also exposed the gap between scientific innovation and operational readiness. Although pan-filovirus diagnostics, investigational vaccines, therapeutics, and adaptive clinical trial platforms are now available, their deployment has been constrained by delayed diagnosis, limited access to species-inclusive diagnostics, insecurity due to conflict, population displacement, and fragile health systems. In this Review, we synthesise evidence on BDBV from its discovery to the current 2026 outbreak, highlighting advances in epidemiology, clinical management, diagnostics, vaccines, therapeutics, and preparedness. More broadly, the outbreak shows that scientific innovation alone is insufficient; its public health impact depends on integrated, species-inclusive systems capable of rapidly detecting, evaluating, and responding to outbreaks caused by any human-pathogenic Orthoebolavirus spp.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本次审查重点关注刚果民主共和国和乌干达由 BDBV 引起的本迪布焦病毒 (BDBV) 和 埃博拉病毒病 的 2026 暴发。中心问题涉及流行病防范的经验教训,包括 BDBV 的 流行病学、发病机制、诊断、临床谱、管理和对策。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述综合了 BDBV 从 2007 年发现到 2026 年 暴发 的证据。它不是对明确数据库、检索日期或研究计数的系统综述,而是对现有证据的叙述性综合。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,仅靠科学创新不足以产生公共卫生影响;需要综合的、包含物种的系统来快速检测、评估和应对由任何人类致病性正埃博拉病毒物种引起的 暴发。2026 年 暴发 暴露了创新和运营准备之间的差距。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究 BDBV 的机会有限,导致在定义其 流行病学、发病机制、诊断、临床谱和最佳管理方面存在差距。暴发 还强调了由于 诊断 延迟、获得物种包容性诊断的机会有限、不安全、人口流离失所和脆弱的卫生系统而在部署诊断、疫苗 和治疗方面面临的挑战。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 优先事项包括制定针对特定物种的对策、改善获得包括物种在内的诊断的机会、加强 暴发 多发地区的卫生系统以及确保快速部署可用工具。该审查强调需要能够应对任何人类致病性正埃博拉病毒的集成系统。

abstract_zh: 刚果民主共和国和乌干达正在发生的由本迪布焦病毒 (BDBV) 引起的 2026 暴发 或 埃博拉病毒病 疫情再次引起人们对研究最少的人类致病性正埃博拉病毒之一的关注。自 2007 年在乌干达西部发现以来,仅报道了两种公认的 BDBV 暴发,限制了定义 流行病学、发病机制、诊断、临床谱和 BDBV 最佳管理或制定物种特异性对策的机会。当前的暴发被世界卫生组织于2026年5月17日宣布为国际关注的突发公共卫生事件,也暴露了科学创新与行动准备之间的差距。尽管泛丝状病毒诊断、研究性 疫苗、治疗方法和适应性临床试验平台现已可用,但其部署受到 诊断 延迟、获得物种包容性诊断的机会有限、冲突造成的不安全、人口流离失所和脆弱的卫生系统的限制。在这篇综述中,我们综合了 BDBV 从发现到当前 2026 年 暴发 的证据,重点介绍了 流行病学、临床管理、诊断、疫苗、治疗和准备方面的进展。更广泛地说,暴发 表明仅靠科学创新是不够的;其公共卫生影响取决于综合的、包含物种的系统,该系统能够快速检测、评估和响应由任何人类致病性正埃博拉病毒属引起的 暴发。

title: Development and characterization of a recombinant Bundibugyo virus expressing a fluorescent reporter protein.
abstract: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with previous outbreaks reporting case fatality rates of 30%-50%. The ongoing BDBV outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda highlights the urgent need for virus-specific research tools and medical countermeasures. Unlike Ebola virus disease caused by Zaire ebolavirus, no licensed vaccines or specific therapeutics are currently available for BVD. The lack of research tools has limited studies with BDBV. To facilitate antiviral testing and neutralization studies, we developed the first recombinant BDBV expressing the fluorescent reporter protein ZsGreen (rBDBV-ZsG). As a proof of concept, we tested a set of previously characterized antiviral compounds and demonstrated comparable inhibitory profiles between rBDBV-ZsG and the wild-type BDBV parental strain. Furthermore, the utility of rBDBV-ZsG was successfully evaluated in neutralization assays, demonstrating robust sensitivity and specificity using monoclonal antibodies and convalescent serum samples.

Unlike Ebola virus disease caused by Zaire ebolavirus, no licensed vaccines or specific therapeutics are currently available for BVD. The lack of research tools has limited studies with BDBV. To facilitate antiviral testing and neutralization studies, we developed the first recombinant BDBV expressing the fluorescent reporter protein ZsGreen (rBDBV-ZsG). As a proof of concept, we tested a set of previously characterized antiviral compounds and demonstrated comparable inhibitory profiles between rBDBV-ZsG and the wild-type BDBV parental strain. Furthermore, the utility of rBDBV-ZsG was successfully evaluated in neutralization assays, demonstrating robust sensitivity and specificity using monoclonal antibodies and convalescent serum samples.
title_original: Development and characterization of a recombinant Bundibugyo virus expressing a fluorescent reporter protein.

analysis.methods: The recombinant virus was tested with previously characterized antiviral compounds to compare inhibitory profiles with the wild-type BDBV parental strain, and its utility was evaluated in neutralization assays using monoclonal antibodies and convalescent serum samples.
analysis.main_results: The recombinant BDBV-ZsG demonstrated comparable inhibitory profiles to the wild-type BDBV and showed robust sensitivity and specificity in neutralization assays with monoclonal antibodies and convalescent serum samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The development of rBDBV-ZsGreen provides a valuable tool for antiviral testing and neutralization studies, addressing the previous limitation of lacking research tools for BDBV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This recombinant virus can accelerate the development of medical countermeasures for BVD by enabling efficient screening of antiviral compounds and evaluation of immune responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study demonstrates proof of concept for the recombinant virus but does not report in vivo testing or clinical applications; the evidence strength is moderate due to the limited scope of validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed the first recombinant Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) expressing a fluorescent reporter protein (rBDBV-ZsG) to address the lack of research tools for BVD, which has high case fatality rates and no licensed treatments. This tool will facilitate antiviral testing and neutralization studies, accelerating the development of medical countermeasures for BVD. The study provides proof of concept but has not yet been tested in vivo or clinical settings.

title: What does a health-zone case-fatality ratio measure during an active outbreak? Reported mortality, mapped health-facility context, and case-death reporting heterogeneity in the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic in DR Congo
abstract: Abstract Background During an active outbreak, deaths divided by confirmed cases can be mistaken for biological severity or quality of care even though outcomes remain unresolved and reporting and ascertainment differ across places. We examined what health-zone case-fatality ratios measured during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Methodology/Principal Findings We analysed national and health-zone cumulative confirmed cases and deaths through 20 July 2026. We calculated reported crude case-fatality ratios, examined case-death reporting synchronisation, and fitted beta-binomial partial-pooling models with four-chain Markov chain Monte Carlo. Exploratory models added mapped clinical-facility availability or distance to the nearest mapped hospital. Reporting-date delay, under-ascertainment, and mortality forecasting were evaluated as diagnostics, scenarios, or developmental analyses rather than patient-level fatality estimation. The national ratio reached 40.4% (999/2,473). Among 14 zones with at least 20 cases, crude ratios ranged from 28.3% to 68.5%. In the primary model, North Kivu had higher posterior odds than Ituri, but with substantial uncertainty (OR 1.80, 95% credible interval 0.92-3.37); epidemic maturity was positively associated (1.49, 1.04-2.19). In exploratory models, greater mapped clinical-facility availability was associated with lower reported fatality (0.67, 0.48-0.96), while greater distance to a mapped hospital was associated with higher reported fatality (1.46, 1.06-2.00). Same-day case-death co-reporting was common, and materially different reporting-delay assumptions fitted similarly. Conclusions/Significance Health-zone ratios revealed meaningful surveillance heterogeneity but did not identify biological fatality risk or causal effects of facilities, access, care, or conflict. Epidemic maturity, selective ascertainment, referral, and administrative reporting plausibly shaped the numerator and denominator. These ratios should guide investigation rather than rank health-zone performance; linked patient records are required for clinical fatality and competing-risks analyses. Author Summary We studied why reported deaths divided by confirmed cases differed so widely between health zones during the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We found that these ratios were strongly influenced by when an outbreak began locally, how cases and deaths entered situation reports, and which cases were detected. The ratio increased nationally as the outbreak matured, and cases and deaths were often added on the same reporting date. Mapped health-facility indicators provided useful clues after statistical adjustment, but they did not measure whether services were open, staffed, equipped, reachable, or capable of treating this disease. The difference between North Kivu and Ituri may partly reflect chronic isolation, referral disruption, distrust, case selection, or reporting, but the available data cannot assign a causal explanation. We conclude that a high health-zone ratio should prompt investigation, not be treated as a ranking of care quality. To determine the actual probability of death and the role of treatment or access, researchers need linked patient records containing clinical dates, outcomes, referral histories, and treatments.

title: How Predictable Was the 2026 Bundibugyo Virus Disease Outbreak? A Rolling-Origin Evaluation of Short-Term Forecast Models, an Empirically Recalibrated Bayesian Model, and a Data-Driven Baseline–Bayesian Ensemble, Using Daily Surveillance Data
abstract: BackgroundThe 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo generated the largest recorded epidemic caused by Bundibugyo virus and displayed unusually rapid early growth. Early scenario projections warned that the outbreak could become one of the largest Ebola-family epidemics on record, but were calibrated to assumed mortality totals and intervention scenarios rather than evaluated repeatedly against subsequently observed daily surveillance data. We assessed how accurately the outbreak could have been forecast in real time using routinely published national situation reports, whether a simple ensemble of two complementary models improved on either alone, and how the resulting forecasts and their uncertainty should be interpreted for operational capacity planning. MethodsWe conducted a retrospective, pseudo-prospective rolling-origin forecasting study using daily cumulative confirmed cases and deaths reported in national situation reports from 14 May to 20 July 2026 (68 calendar days; 61 numeric national reports). Every date with a newly reported national total became an eligible forecast origin once at least seven numeric observations were available (55 origins). At each origin, all later observations were withheld and two prespecified operational models were refitted using only data available at that time: a recent seven-increment baseline and a Bayesian negative-binomial surveillance-maturity model fitted by full Markov Chain Monte Carlo on complete available history. A Gompertz growth model was also fitted identically at every origin as a phenomenological benchmark. Forecasts were generated for 7-, 14-, and 21-day horizons and evaluated only when an observation existed on the exact target date. The Bayesian models forecasts were additionally corrected by a prospective, quality-gated empirical recalibration using only errors already realised at earlier, forecast-maturity-qualified origins. We further evaluated a data-driven ensemble that pooled the baselines bootstrap trajectories with the recalibrated Bayesian models posterior predictive trajectories, with horizon- and outcome-specific mixing weights selected by a strictly prospective, expanding-origin procedure using an explicit asymmetric operational loss function. FindingsA statistical and externally corroborated surveillance-maturity discontinuity was identified on 28 May 2026 (robust z-score 13{middle dot}0 against the trailing week). The Gompertz model had the poorest 80% predictive-interval coverage of all candidates at every horizon and outcome (25{middle dot}9-34{middle dot}1% for cases, 0{middle dot}0-23{middle dot}5% for deaths) and is reported as tested and excluded. Recalibration corrected a directionally consistent Bayesian underprediction tendency and is the primary reported Bayesian result; the correction was applied at 24 of 55 origins for the 21-day horizon (never at 28 days in earlier work), because 21-day forecasts reach the forecast-maturity threshold (mature history [≥] forecast horizon) from the 18 June origin onward, a genuinely more useful operational horizon than 28 days. Recalibration improved case coverage substantially (7-day 80% coverage 60{middle dot}0%[->]80{middle dot}0%; 14-day 41{middle dot}0%[->]76{middle dot}9%) and improved death forecasts on both accuracy and calibration (7-day median absolute percentage error 10{middle dot}3%[->]7{middle dot}7%; 80% coverage 33{middle dot}3%[->]95{middle dot}6%). The baseline-Bayesian ensembles evidence-selected weighting differed materially by outcome: for cases, the operationally and distributionally optimal blend was baseline-heavy (w{approx}0{middle dot}8-0{middle dot}9 toward the baseline) at every horizon; for deaths, the optimal blend was close to parity (w{approx}0{middle dot}5-0{middle dot}6), and the ensemble improved mean weighted interval score over both individual component models at every horizon (e.g., 7-day: baseline 24{middle dot}8, Bayesian 20{middle dot}5, ensemble 17{middle dot}9). InterpretationRoutine SitRep data supported useful short-term forecasting, but no single model was best on every criterion, and a data-driven combination of two complementary, individually weaker-in-some-respect models measurably outperformed either alone for one of two outcomes evaluated. Three distinct kinds of maturity determine whether a forecast at a given horizon can be trusted: epidemic maturity, surveillance maturity, and forecast maturity; the last of these is the strongest and most model-agnostic finding in this paper, and motivates reporting 21- rather than 28-day forecasts as the longest routine operational horizon. We report an explicit, reproducible, and adjustable framework -- not a fixed recommendation -- for combining simple and complex models and for communicating the resulting uncertainty to non-specialist operational decision-makers. Funding: none received specifically for this analysis. Author SummaryWhen an outbreak is growing, planners need to know not just how many cases to expect, but how much to trust that number. We tested, in a fully retrospective and fair way, how well three forecasting methods -- a simple recent-trend method, a saturating growth curve, and a more sophisticated probabilistic model -- could have predicted the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo one, two, and three weeks ahead, using only the information that would genuinely have been available at each point in time. The saturating growth-curve model performed worst on every measure and is not recommended. The simple trend method gave the most accurate single-number forecasts for confirmed cases, but its stated uncertainty ranges were frequently wrong. The probabilistic models ranges were much better calibrated once we corrected a systematic bias using only past, already-known forecast errors -- a technique we describe in enough detail that others can reuse it on their own outbreaks. Combining the simple and probabilistic methods, in carefully validated proportions that differ for cases and for deaths, produced better forecasts than either method alone for deaths specifically. We also explain, in plain language, what a forecasts uncertainty range does and does not mean for a non-statistician planning hospital beds, staff, or supplies, and we show that three-week forecasts are far more trustworthy than four-week ones simply because the outbreak had not yet generated enough mature surveillance history to test a four-week forecast fairly -- a checkable data limitation, not a permanent weakness of any model.

analysis.main_results: The Gompertz model had the poorest 80% predictive-interval coverage of all candidates at every horizon and outcome (25.9-34.1% for cases, 0.0-23.5% for deaths). analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was retrospective and pseudo-prospective, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on historical data and the absence of prospective validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the predictability of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo using retrospective forecasting models. The researchers tested three methods—a simple recent-trend baseline, a Bayesian surveillance-maturity model, and a Gompertz growth curve—using daily surveillance data. The Gompertz model performed poorly, while recalibration significantly improved the Bayesian model's accuracy. A data-driven ensemble combining the baseline and Bayesian models outperformed individual models for case forecasts. The study highlights the importance of epidemic, surveillance, and forecast maturity in determining forecast reliability and provides a reproducible framework for communicating uncertainty to decision-makers.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 2026 年刚果民主共和国的本迪布焦病毒病 暴发 造成了有记录以来最大规模的由本迪布焦病毒引起的流行病,并表现出异常快速的早期增长,促使人们对 暴发 的实时预测准确度进行评估。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们利用 2026 年 5 月 14 日至 7 月 20 日(68 个日历日;61 份数字国家报告)国家形势报告中报告的每日累计确诊病例和死亡人数进行了一项回顾性、伪前瞻性滚动来源预测研究。
elements_zh.methods: 我们评估了两个预先指定的操作模型(最近的七增量基线和贝叶斯负二项式 监测 成熟度模型)和 Gompertz 增长模型作为基准,生成 7 天、14 天和 21 天范围内的预测,并且仅在确切目标日期存在观测时进行评估。
elements_zh.main_results: Gompertz 模型对所有候选者在每个范围和结果的 80% 预测区间覆盖率最差(病例为 25.9-34.1%,死亡为 0.0-23.5%)。重新校准大大提高了病例覆盖率(7天80%覆盖率60.0%→80.0%;14天41.0%→76.9%),并提高了死亡预测的准确性和校准率(7天中位绝对百分比误差10.3%→7.7%;80%覆盖率33.3%→95.6%)。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 我们报告了一个明确的、可重复的和可调整的框架,用于组合简单和复杂的模型,并将由此产生的不确定性传达给非专业运营决策者,并用三种不同的成熟度来确定给定范围内的预测是否可信。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是回顾性和伪前瞻性的,由于依赖历史数据且缺乏前瞻性验证,证据强度中等。

title: A panel of biologically contained orthoebolaviruses for the screening of broad-spectrum antivirals
abstract: Abstract Filoviruses, particularly those of the Orthoebolavirus genus, pose ongoing public health threats due to their increasing frequency and geographic spread. However, research has been impeded by the biosafety level 4 classification of filoviruses. We previously reported the generation of biologically contained Ebola, Marburg and Sudan virus as lower biosafety level-compatible filovirus systems. In the present study, we expanded this repertoire to include biologically contained Taï Forest, Bundibugyo and Reston virus, thereby creating a near-complete toolkit for currently recognized human-relevant orthoebolaviruses. VP30-deficient viruses were generated with matching VP30 expressing cell lines. More specifically, we developed and optimized a dual-reporter system in VeroE6, Huh-7 and A549 cells, combining a virus-encoded enhanced green fluorescent protein reporter as readout for viral replication with a stably cellular-expressed nuclear mCherry marker for cytotoxicity assessment. Next, we screened two repurposing-oriented compound libraries comprising 640 small molecules against Taï Forest, Bundibugyo and Sudan virus, and subsequently cross-validated against Reston and Ebola virus. This approach identified multiple candidates with broad-spectrum activity across orthoebolaviruses, while also revealing virus-specific antivirals, with robust activity observed in both primate- and human-derived cell lines. Together, this work establishes a versatile and experimentally tractable lower biosafety level-compatible platform for the study of human-relevant orthoebolaviruses and the systematic discovery of broad-spectrum antiviral countermeasures against filoviruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Filoviruses in the Orthoebolavirus genus are recognized public-health threats, but their BSL-4 containment has impeded research and antiviral discovery.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study expanded a panel of biologically contained orthoebolaviruses to include Taï Forest, Bundibugyo and Reston virus, creating a near-complete toolkit for human-relevant orthoebolaviruses.
analysis.methods: VP30-deficient viruses were generated and matched to VP30-expressing cell lines, and a dual-reporter system in VeroE6, Huh-7 and A549 cells was developed to quantify replication via EGFP and cytotoxicity via nuclear mCherry.
analysis.main_results: Screening of two repurposing-oriented compound libraries (640 small molecules) identified multiple candidates with broad-spectrum activity across orthoebolaviruses and virus-specific antivirals, with robust activity in both primate- and human-derived cell lines.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The work establishes a versatile, lower BSL-compatible platform for studying human-relevant orthoebolaviruses and systematically discovering broad-spectrum antiviral countermeasures against filoviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This platform enables standardized, high-throughput screening of antivirals against multiple orthoebolaviruses without BSL-4 containment, accelerating countermeasure development.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro systems and does not evaluate in vivo efficacy or safety, so the evidence strength is moderate and requires downstream validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the public-health need for safer, lower-containment tools to study orthoebolaviruses by expanding a panel of biologically contained viruses to include Taï Forest, Bundibugyo and Reston virus, thereby creating a near-complete toolkit for human-relevant orthoebolaviruses. The authors developed a dual-reporter system in multiple cell lines to quantify replication and cytotoxicity and screened two repurposing-oriented compound libraries (640 small molecules) to identify broad-spectrum antivirals and virus-specific candidates with robust activity in primate- and human-derived cells. The work establishes a versatile, lower biosafety level-compatible platform for systematic antiviral discovery against filoviruses, though in vitro-only evidence limits the strength of conclusions and necessitates in vivo validation.

abstract_zh: 摘要 丝状病毒,特别是正埃博拉病毒属的丝状病毒,由于其频率的增加和地理传播的不断增加,对公共卫生构成持续威胁。然而,丝状病毒生物安全4级分类阻碍了研究。我们之前报道了生物安全水平较低的丝状病毒系统中包含的埃博拉病毒、马尔堡病毒和苏丹病毒的产生。在本研究中,我们扩展了这一库,包括生物上包含的塔伊森林病毒、本迪布焦病毒和雷斯顿病毒,从而为目前公认的人类相关正埃博拉病毒创建了一个近乎完整的工具包。VP30 缺陷型病毒是用匹配的 VP30 表达细胞系生成的。更具体地说,我们在 VeroE6、Huh-7 和 A549 细胞中开发并优化了双报告基因系统,将病毒编码的增强型绿色荧光蛋白报告基因(作为病毒复制的读数)与稳定细胞表达的核 mCherry 标记(用于细胞毒性评估)相结合。接下来,我们针对 Taï Forest、Bundibugyo 和苏丹病毒筛选了两个包含 640 个小分子的面向再利用的化合物库,随后针对 Reston 和 埃博拉病毒 进行交叉验证。这种方法鉴定了多个在正埃博拉病毒中具有广谱活性的候选物,同时还揭示了病毒特异性的 抗病毒药物,在灵长类和人类来源的细胞系中观察到了强大的活性。总之,这项工作建立了一个多功能且实验上易于处理的较低生物安全水平兼容平台,用于研究人类相关的正埃博拉病毒和系统地发现针对丝状病毒的广谱 抗病毒药物 对策。

title: Digital Health for Pandemic Preparedness: A Critical Review of Innovations, Equity Gaps, and Governance in Infectious Disease Surveillance
abstract: Context: Recent infectious disease emergencies, including SARS-CoV-2, mpox (2022 - 2024), highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in US dairy cattle (2024 - 2025), and the Marburg virus in Rwanda (2024), have strained traditional surveillance systems. Digital health has been proposed as a paradigm shift; however, most reviews have focused on diagnostic accuracy while neglecting equity and governance. Evidence Acquisition: We conducted a structured thematic narrative review of peer-reviewed and grey literature published from January 2010 to March 2025, reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from February 5 to 18, 2025. Search keywords combined three concept blocks: (1) Digital-health technologies (artificial intelligence, machine learning, mHealth, eHealth, telemedicine, electronic health records, wearables, wastewater surveillance, genomic surveillance, natural-language processing); (2) infectious diseases (outbreak, pandemic, epidemic, COVID-19, Ebola, Zika, mpox, influenza, antimicrobial resistance, Marburg); and (3) public-health functions (surveillance, detection, forecasting, contact tracing, governance, equity). Full Boolean syntax is provided. Records were deduplicated in EndNote X20 and screened by 2 blinded reviewers in Rayyan (Cohen κ = 0.81). Empirical studies were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool 2018, and reviews were appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. The synthesis followed Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis and was interpreted through sociotechnical systems and data justice lenses. Results: Of 1498 records, 142 studies met the inclusion criteria; 48% (69/142) were rated as high quality. The evidence base was heavily skewed regionally (high-income countries [HICs], 41%; sub-Saharan Africa or South Asia, 19%). No technology was universally superior. Artificial intelligence (AI) studies were concentrated in HICs (18/32, 56%), whereas short-message-service (SMS) mHealth studies were concentrated in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs; 15/25, 60%). Recurring barriers included algorithmic bias, fragmented interoperability, donor-dependent sustainability, and slow benefit-sharing of pathogen data with LMICs. Conclusions: Across 142 included studies the synthesis supports a measured conclusion: Digital health is necessary but not sufficient for pandemic preparedness. The patterns most consistently observed in the evidence — regional skew, recurring governance failures, donor-dependent sustainability, and design choices that determine equity outcomes — together indicate that equity, sustainability, and accountability are constituents of effectiveness rather than obstacles to it. The binding constraint is increasingly political and institutional will rather than analytic uncertainty.

title: Exploration of BoltzGen permeable cyclic-minipeptides targeting Ebola GP2 prefusion-state
abstract: Cyclic-minipeptide-conformer candidates were co-generated by targeting ebo la v irus (EBOV) GP2 prefusion trimer-interfaces implicated in pH-dependent fusion to host-endosomal membranes. GP2 trimer, dimer and NHR α-helix interfaces were independently targeted by BoltzGen co-generating candidates predicting nanoMolar-high affinities and membrane-permeabilities. Cyclic-minipeptides would provide easy chemical synthesis and high environmental / endoprotease stabilities which may facilitate in vitro and animal-model validations. Therefore, permeable cyclic-minipeptide candidates may be instrumental to computational-guide further developments toward EBOV-specific drugs. Because their many contacts to GP2 highly conserved amino acids, some of these may be also candidates to EBOV pan-variants and avoid crossreactivities with pan-hemorragic fever viral diseases and/or highly-abundant proteins in human fluids

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop cyclic-minipeptide candidates targeting Ebola virus GP2 prefusion trimer-interfaces to inhibit pH-dependent fusion to host-endosomal membranes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research focused on computational design of cyclic-minipeptides targeting Ebola virus GP2 trimer, dimer, and NHR α-helix interfaces.
analysis.methods: BoltzGen co-generation was used to design cyclic-minipeptides predicting nanoMolar-high affinities and membrane-permeabilities, with emphasis on chemical synthesis feasibility and environmental stability.
analysis.main_results: Cyclic-minipeptide candidates were predicted to have high affinities and membrane-permeabilities, with potential for broad EBOV variant coverage and minimal crossreactivity with other viral diseases or human proteins.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these candidates as instrumental for computational-guided development of EBOV-specific drugs, leveraging their stability and predicted efficacy against conserved GP2 regions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These permeable cyclic-minipeptides could facilitate in vitro and animal-model validations, advancing the development of targeted therapeutics for Ebola virus disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is computational and preclinical, with no experimental validation reported; confidence is moderate due to the lack of empirical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study explored cyclic-minipeptide candidates targeting Ebola virus GP2 prefusion trimer-interfaces to inhibit viral fusion. Using BoltzGen co-generation, the researchers designed peptides predicting high affinities and membrane-permeabilities, with potential for broad EBOV variant coverage and minimal crossreactivity. The candidates offer advantages in chemical synthesis and stability, supporting future in vitro and animal-model validations. While computationally promising, the lack of experimental validation limits current confidence in their therapeutic potential.

title: It’s not just virology: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda demands a wider public health response
abstract: The current outbreak of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus (species Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda is much more than another infectious disease emergency. It reminds us that epidemics come not only from biological pathogens but also from social inequities, environmental disruption, fragile health systems, and persistent armed conflict. While Ebola captures headlines because of its fear-provoking symptoms and high mortality, the conditions that allow it to spread receive far less attention.

title: ONE CHAIN, REPEATED SPILLOVER, OR AN UNRELATED EARLY SIGNAL?
abstract: Abstract Background: A retrospective field investigation described substantial illness and mortality in and around Mongbwalu from January 2026, several months before Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) was formally recognised in May. Historical BDBV evidence includes a genomic reconstruction compatible with multiple spillovers, while other orthoebolavirus outbreaks have involved survivor-associated resurgence, concurrent lineages and substantial syndromic misclassification. We evaluated whether the early Mongbwalu signal was most compatible with continuous acute transmission, a later introduction, survivor-mediated reseeding, or mixed/non-ancestral mortality. Methods: We combined a structured rapid review of 35 sources with official confirmed surveillance, a published report of an unpublished retrospective investigation, and a soft genomic timing constraint. A resample-move approximate Bayesian computation sequential Monte Carlo model simulated 20 weekly periods across Mongbwalu, Bunia, Rwampara and Nizi. Four hypotheses were compared: continuous acute transmission (H1), repeated zoonotic introduction or temporarily elevated shared exposure (H2), survivor-mediated sexual transmission from persistent virus in semen (H3), and mixed or substantially non-ancestral retrospective mortality (H4). Three independent chains of 450 particles were run for each hypothesis over seven decreasing tolerances. Model recovery, prior sensitivity, posterior-predictive checks and leave-one-component-out analyses assessed identifiability and robustness. Results: Under equal priors, H4 received 36.2%, H2 32.6%, H3 21.6% and H1 9.6%. Under the literature-neutral prior, H2 received 50.0%, H4 34.7%, H1 11.1% and H3 4.2%. H2 and H4 jointly accounted for 84.8% under the main prior and 68.7%-89.3% across all prior families, demonstrating a robust preference for a discontinuous origin history. The approximate evidence ratio was only 1.11:1 for H4 over H2, so H2's lead under the main analysis reflected both close empirical fit and direct BDBV precedent incorporated into the prior. H1 was correctly recovered in 92% of equal-prior synthetic datasets, compared with 52% for H2, 42% for H3 and 24% for H4. Removing confirmed May counts eliminated H2's clear advantage, identifying the rapid May expansion as the principal evidence for a later successful seed. Interpretation: The findings favour a discontinuous origin: the January/February Mongbwalu signal was epidemiologically meaningful, but the lineage that expanded in May most probably arose from a later successful introduction or renewed primary exposure rather than from one uninterrupted acute chain. H2 is the preferred literature-informed explanation because it best reconciles the structured early signal, March-centred sampled ancestry and rapid May growth, while direct BDBV precedent makes the mechanism credible. H4 remains a substantial alternative because the early events were not laboratory confirmed and H2 and H4 are only partly identifiable. H3 is temporally and biologically possible but lacks survivor-specific evidence, and H1 is not the leading explanation under any tested prior family.

title_zh: 一条链,重复的 跨物种溢出,还是不相关的早期信号?
source_body_en: Abstract Background: A retrospective field investigation described substantial illness and mortality in and around Mongbwalu from January 2026, several months before Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) was formally recognised in May. Historical BDBV evidence includes a genomic reconstruction compatible with multiple spillovers, while other orthoebolavirus outbreaks have involved survivor-associated resurgence, concurrent lineages and substantial syndromic misclassification. We evaluated whether the early Mongbwalu signal was most compatible with continuous acute transmission, a later introduction, survivor-mediated reseeding, or mixed/non-ancestral mortality. Methods: We combined a structured rapid review of 35 sources with official confirmed surveillance, a published report of an unpublished retrospective investigation, and a soft genomic timing constraint. A resample-move approximate Bayesian computation sequential Monte Carlo model simulated 20 weekly periods across Mongbwalu, Bunia, Rwampara and Nizi. Four hypotheses were compared: continuous acute transmission (H1), repeated zoonotic introduction or temporarily elevated shared exposure (H2), survivor-mediated sexual transmission from persistent virus in semen (H3), and mixed or substantially non-ancestral retrospective mortality (H4). Three independent chains of 450 particles were run for each hypothesis over seven decreasing tolerances. Model recovery, prior sensitivity, posterior-predictive checks and leave-one-component-out analyses assessed identifiability and robustness. Results: Under equal priors, H4 received 36.2%, H2 32.6%, H3 21.6% and H1 9.6%. Under the literature-neutral prior, H2 received 50.0%, H4 34.7%, H1 11.1% and H3 4.2%. H2 and H4 jointly accounted for 84.8% under the main prior and 68.7%-89.3% across all prior families, demonstrating a robust preference for a discontinuous origin history. The approximate evidence ratio was only 1.11:1 for H4 over H2, so H2's lead under the main analysis reflected both close empirical fit and direct BDBV precedent incorporated into the prior. H1 was correctly recovered in 92% of equal-prior synthetic datasets, compared with 52% for H2, 42% for H3 and 24% for H4. Removing confirmed May counts eliminated H2's clear advantage, identifying the rapid May expansion as the principal evidence for a later successful seed. Interpretation: The findings favour a discontinuous origin: the January/February Mongbwalu signal was epidemiologically meaningful, but the lineage that expanded in May most probably arose from a later successful introduction or renewed primary exposure rather than from one uninterrupted acute chain. H2 is the preferred literature-informed explanation because it best reconciles the structured early signal, March-centred sampled ancestry and rapid May growth, while direct BDBV precedent makes the mechanism credible. H4 remains a substantial alternative because the early events were not laboratory confirmed and H2 and H4 are only partly identifiable. H3 is temporally and biologically possible but lacks survivor-specific evidence, and H1 is not the leading explanation under any tested prior family.
abstract_zh: 摘要背景:一项回顾性现场调查描述了自 2026 年 1 月起,即本迪布焦病毒病 (BVD) 于 5 月正式确认的几个月后,Mongbwalu 及其周边地区出现了严重疾病和 死亡率。历史 BDBV 证据包括与多个 跨物种溢出 兼容的基因组重建,而其他正埃博拉病毒 暴发 涉及幸存者相关的复苏、并发谱系和严重的综合征错误分类。我们评估了早期 Mongbwalu 信号是否与连续急性 传播、后来的引入、幸存者介导的重新播种或混合/非祖先 死亡率 最兼容。方法:我们将 35 个来源的结构化快速审查与官方确认的 监测、未发表的回顾性调查的已发表报告以及软基因组时间约束结合起来。重采样移动近似贝叶斯计算顺序蒙特卡罗模型模拟了 Mongbwalu、Bunia、Rwampara 和 Nizi 的 20 个每周周期。比较了四种假设:持续急性 传播 (H1)、重复人畜共患病引入或暂时升高的共同暴露 (H2)、精液中持续病毒引起的幸存者介导的性 传播 (H3) 以及混合或基本上非祖先的回顾性 死亡率 (H4)。针对每个假设运行 3 个由 450 个粒子组成的独立链,超过七个递减的公差。模型恢复、先验敏感性、后验预测检查和留一成分分析评估了可识别性和稳健性。结果:在同等先验条件下,H4 获得 36.2%,H2 获得 32.6%,H3 获得 21.6%,H1 获得 9.6%。在文献中性的先验条件下,H2 为 50.0%,H4 为 34.7%,H1 为 11.1%,H3 为 4.2%。H2 和 H4 在主要先验家族中共同占 84.8%,在所有先验家族中占 68.7%-89.3%,这表明对不连续起源历史的强烈偏好。H4 相对于 H2 的近似证据比仅为 1.11:1,因此 H2 在主要分析中的领先反映了紧密的经验拟合和直接纳入先验的 BDBV 先例。在 92% 的同等先验合成数据集中,H1 被正确恢复,而 H2 为 52%,H3 为 42%,H4 为 24%。删除已确认的 5 月计数消除了 H2 的明显优势,将 5 月的快速扩张确定为后来成功种子的主要证据。解释:研究结果支持不连续的起源:1月/2月的Mongbwalu信号具有流行病学意义,但5月扩展的谱系很可能源自后来的成功引入或新的初次接触,而不是来自一个不间断的急性链。H2 是首选的基于文献的解释,因为它最好地协调了结构化的早期信号、以 3 月为中心的采样祖先和 5 月的快速增长,而直接的 BDBV 先例使该机制变得可信。H4 仍然是一个重要的替代方案,因为早期事件未经实验室证实,并且 H2 和 H4 仅部分可识别。H3 在时间上和生物学上都是可能的,但缺乏幸存者特定的证据,并且 H1 并不是任何测试过的先前家庭的主要解释。

title: Potential Mechanisms Underlying Bleeding During Infection With Hemorrhagic Fever Viruses.
abstract: Viral hemorrhagic fever (VHF) describes different diseases caused by several viruses from 6 virus families: Filoviridae , Nairoviridae , Phenuiviridae , Hepadnaviridae , Arenaviridae , and Flaviviridae . VHF was once considered a geographically localized problem, but, due to expanding vector ranges and increased human contact with animal reservoirs and hosts, the number of VHF cases is increasing. As the name indicates, VHF is associated with bleeding. Both direct effects from viral infection of host cells and indirect effects caused by the host response to the virus contribute to the dysregulation of the hemostatic system. Many studies have measured different parameters and various biomarkers in samples from infected humans and nonhuman primate models. For example, Ebola virus infection in a nonhuman primate model leads to increased TF (tissue factor) expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and extracellular vesicles. In dengue virus infection, thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction occur. There are likely both common and distinct mechanisms underlying bleeding in different VHFs, as sites of bleeding differ between the viruses. Herein, we discuss the potential mechanisms leading to bleeding during VHF, which include a consumptive coagulopathy, decreased coagulation factor production, thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction, and endothelial cell activation and damage, resulting in increased vascular permeability. While a significant body of work exists examining different aspects of the various viral infections that may lead to bleeding, there are still many open questions and areas for investigation. Therefore, more studies are needed to better understand the mechanisms underlying bleeding in VHF caused by different viruses.

Many studies have measured different parameters and various biomarkers in samples from infected humans and nonhuman primate models. For example, Ebola virus infection in a nonhuman primate model leads to increased TF (tissue factor) expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and extracellular vesicles. In dengue virus infection, thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction occur. There are likely both common and distinct mechanisms underlying bleeding in different VHFs, as sites of bleeding differ between the viruses. Herein, we discuss the potential mechanisms leading to bleeding during VHF, which include a consumptive coagulopathy, decreased coagulation factor production, thrombocytopenia and platelet dysfunction, and endothelial cell activation and damage, resulting in increased vascular permeability. While a significant body of work exists examining different aspects of the various viral infections that may lead to bleeding, there are still many open questions and areas for investigation. Therefore, more studies are needed to better understand the mechanisms underlying bleeding in VHF caused by different viruses.

abstract_zh: 病毒性出血热 (VHF) 是由 6 个病毒科的几种病毒引起的不同疾病:丝状病毒科、内罗病毒科、苯丙病毒科、嗜肝DNA病毒科、沙粒病毒科和黄病毒科。VHF 曾经被认为是一个地理局部问题,但是,由于 媒介 范围的扩大以及人类与动物 储存宿主 和 宿主 接触的增加,VHF 病例的数量正在增加。顾名思义,VHF 与出血有关。宿主 细胞病毒感染的直接影响和 宿主 对病毒反应引起的间接影响都会导致止血系统的失调。许多研究测量了受感染人类和非人类灵长类动物模型样本中的不同参数和各种生物标志物。例如,非人灵长类动物模型中的 埃博拉病毒 感染导致外周血单核细胞和细胞外囊泡中 TF(组织因子)表达增加。登革热病毒感染时,会出现血小板减少和血小板功能障碍。不同甚高频的出血可能存在共同和不同的机制,因为不同病毒的出血部位不同。在此,我们讨论导致 VHF 期间出血的潜在机制,包括消耗性凝血病、凝血因子产生减少、血小板减少和血小板功能障碍,以及内皮细胞活化和损伤,导致血管通透性增加。尽管有大量工作正在研究可能导致出血的各种病毒感染的不同方面,但仍有许多悬而未决的问题和领域需要调查。因此,需要更多的研究来更好地了解不同病毒引起的甚高频出血的机制。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the clinical characteristics and outcomes of hospital staff admitted with infectious symptoms during the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in DR Congo. This is important due to the potential risk of nosocomial transmission and the need to understand the impact of the outbreak on healthcare workers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cohort study was conducted in Bunia, DR Congo, from April to May 2026, focusing on Congolese hospital staff who were admitted with infectious symptoms during the Bundibugyo virus outbreak. The study included all relevant participants in this setting.
analysis.methods: The study involved data collection from hospital staff admitted with infectious symptoms during the outbreak, followed by analysis of the data to determine clinical characteristics and outcomes. The data were collected and analyzed by the authors as part of their research process.
analysis.main_results: The study reported that all participants were admitted with infectious symptoms, and the majority were diagnosed with Bundibugyo virus. No specific numerical results were provided in the supplied evidence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as highlighting the vulnerability of hospital staff during the Bundibugyo virus outbreak and the importance of implementing protective measures. This study provides novel insights into the clinical manifestations observed in healthcare workers during such outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted protective measures for healthcare workers during outbreaks of Bundibugyo virus and similar pathogens. They also underscore the need for improved surveillance and infection control in healthcare settings during viral outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational nature and the lack of detailed statistical analysis. However, the evidence is strong given the direct observation of clinical symptoms in the context of the Bundibugyo virus outbreak, and the data were collected and analyzed by the authors.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the clinical characteristics and outcomes of Congolese hospital staff admitted with infectious symptoms during the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in Bunia, DR Congo, in April and May 2026. The research highlights the risks faced by healthcare workers in such outbreaks and the importance of protective measures. The study is a cohort analysis, providing insights into the impact of the virus on hospital staff. While the study lacks detailed statistical analysis, the direct observation of symptoms in the outbreak setting supports its findings. The results emphasize the need for improved surveillance and infection control in healthcare environments during viral outbreaks. The evidence is considered moderate due to the observational design and limited data specifics.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查刚果民主共和国本迪布焦病毒 暴发 期间出现感染症状的医院工作人员的临床特征和结果。由于院内 传播 的潜在风险以及需要了解 暴发 对医护人员的影响,这一点很重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2026 年 4 月至 5 月在刚果民主共和国布尼亚进行了一项 队列研究 研究,重点关注在本迪布焦病毒 暴发 期间因感染症状入院的刚果医院工作人员。该研究包括了该环境中的所有相关参与者。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究涉及从 暴发 期间因感染症状入院的医院工作人员收集数据,然后分析数据以确定临床特征和结果。作为研究过程的一部分,作者收集并分析了这些数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究报告称,所有参与者入院时均出现感染症状,其中大多数被诊断患有本迪布焦病毒。所提供的证据中没有提供具体的数字结果。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为强调了医院工作人员在本迪布焦病毒 暴发 期间的脆弱性以及实施保护措施的重要性。这项研究为医护人员在 暴发 期间观察到的临床表现提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为在本迪布焦病毒和类似病原体的 暴发 期间为医护人员制定有针对性的保护措施提供参考。他们还强调在病毒 暴发 期间需要改进医疗机构中的 监测 和感染控制。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其观察性质和缺乏详细的统计分析而受到限制。然而,鉴于在本迪布焦病毒 暴发 的背景下对临床症状的直接观察,证据是强有力的,并且数据是由作者收集和分析的。

full_text: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has declared its seventeenth Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, which had been circulating undetected for months. The response is now catching up across a region weakened by conflict, displacement and loss of humanitarian aid. With no licensed vaccine or treatment, containment will depend on rebuilding resources, access and trust in public health systems. Subjects The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and its neighbouring countries face an incredible challenge in the new Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) disease outbreak. By the time the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale in Kinshasa confirmed BDBV in Ituri Province, officials had already recorded 246 suspected cases and 80 suspected deaths across several health zones. Confirmed cases were soon logged across multiple DRC provinces and in Kampala, the capital of neighbouring Uganda1. The WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May, and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention followed with a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security on 18 May, naming ten other countries at high risk of spread2,3. The scale of those initial figures made it evident that the world was not discovering a new outbreak so much as uncovering one that had been silently circulating, hidden by the fragility of local healthcare capacity and propagated by conflict, community distrust and population mobility. As of 31 May, 336 cases had been confirmed across both countries, with 49 confirmed deaths, alongside 220 suspected cases and 236 suspected deaths in the DRC. These numbers are almost certainly an undercount. A modelling group at Imperial College London estimated within days of the declaration that true infections probably already exceeded 900, and many community deaths have never entered a formal record4. Unlike West Africa in 2013, where the index case seeded a region with no prior filovirus experience, the DRC and its neighbours have extensive experience with viral haemorrhagic fevers, including 10 outbreaks in the past 5 years alone. The communities and health workers of the region have shown remarkable resilience across these repeated emergencies, carrying the burden of response, often at great personal cost, with limited and intermittent external support. However, a confluence of factors is lining up to make this outbreak at least the second-biggest Ebola crisis the world has seen. First, delayed laboratory identification allowed geographic expansion, and the response is now playing catch-up. The initial delay followed negative Ebola testing at the provincial laboratory in Bunia, which required specimens to be sent to Kinshasa for species-specific confirmation. Even before the 5 May alert to the WHO, some unexplained illnesses had been noted in the region with negative testing for common pathogens, highlighting regional blind spots leading to the current crisis, which may have resulted from sudden withdrawal of aid. The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) was historically the DRC’s largest humanitarian donor and since its dissolution the DRC has seen surge in cholera, mpox and measles across its eastern provinces, conditions under which an uncommon disease is far harder to distinguish from the common ones5. Although most cases remain in Ituri, patients have been confirmed hundreds of kilometres away in North and South Kivu Provinces, in eastern DRC. These multiple fronts require already-strained resources — treatment units, infection prevention and sanitation supplies, contact tracers, laboratory capacity and community engagement — to be divided even further. Financial commitments have been made by the national government and the global community, but there is typically a lag between the appropriation of funds and their conversion into contracts, procurement and distribution, making this the most precarious moment of the response. Reports from affected areas indicate that personal protective equipment and diagnostic supplies are severely lagging behind need6. Active conflict is impeding access, and that conflict has worsened with the withdrawal of aid that followed the dismantling of USAID. On 28 May, the WHO Director-General travelled to the DRC to appeal for a ceasefire, enabling central outbreak control efforts to continue: bringing sick patients into isolation, assuring them they will be safe as they receive care, and tracing their contacts across an insecure terrain. In this outbreak, trust is as valuable and critical as monetary funds. A population-based survey during the 2018–2019 North Kivu outbreak found that only about a third of respondents trusted that local authorities represented their interests, and a quarter believed the outbreak was not real7. During that outbreak, the WHO recorded roughly 390 attacks on health facilities and workers in 2019 (ref. 8). The same dynamics are now compounded by displacement and the loss of the previously funded community programmes. Because there have been only two previous outbreaks, research on BDBV medical countermeasures lags between that for Zaire and Sudan ebolaviruses, for which there are either approved products or more products with safety and efficacy data. Although arrangements for vaccine and therapeutic trials are underway, the manufacturing and trial timelines mean deployment is likely to be months away9. Their capacity to alter the trajectory of this outbreak, at least in the near term, is therefore limited. And that trajectory is concerning. The outbreak will probably continue for months, potentially into 2027, with a high risk of spread into areas hosting displaced and refugee populations and across borders, making regional collaboration essential. Although BDBV is unlikely to cause a pandemic, as cases rise, sporadic suspect cases may surface in travellers worldwide, particularly given the nonspecific early symptoms of Ebola. Despite the alarm these cases generate, the base rate of true infection among travellers is very low, and the overwhelming majority of suspected cases evaluated elsewhere will test negative. BDBV mortality has ranged from 30% to 50% in the historical record, lower than the roughly 40–66% seen in large Zaire ebolavirus outbreaks. But those estimates rest on a small number of patients, and case fatality rates shift over the arc of an outbreak. Early mortality may be high, reflecting delays in reaching care and a shortage of treatment resources. As more resources arrive, a falling case fatality rate would indicate two improvements at once: better success in building trust and bringing patients in, and better supportive care once they arrive. The current numbers could be read as a measure of the response’s reach as well as the virus’s lethality. Lastly, the current outbreak is occurring in the middle of another underlying shift: US global aid architecture is shifting towards new approaches, such as ‘America First’ bilateral agreements, rather than investment in multilateral and sector-wide health programmes. African countries are re-examining how regional commitments can be consolidated to build a safer, more self-reliant future10. The containment of Bundibugyo virus outbreak, and the inevitable outbreaks that will follow it, will require consistent commitment on both fronts at once: regional investment that builds standing capacity where these viruses emerge, and global solidarity that is durable rather than episodic. A reactive posture, in which funding is surged only after a crisis has occurred, leaves us backfooted, particularly in areas of complex humanitarian emergencies. This creates massive gaps in timely resources, the cost of which is paid in patient lives and healthcare worker safety. References - World Health Organization. title_original: Bundibugyo virus outbreak: when a concerning pathogen meets a humanitarian emergency.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the challenge of the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring countries, highlighting the public health crisis caused by a pathogen that had been circulating undetected for months in a region weakened by conflict and displacement.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The outbreak was documented across multiple provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and in Kampala, Uganda, with confirmed cases and deaths recorded as of 31 May.
analysis.methods: Laboratory confirmation was delayed due to negative Ebola testing at the provincial laboratory in Bunia, requiring specimens to be sent to Kinshasa for species-specific identification.
analysis.main_results: As of 31 May, 336 cases had been confirmed across both countries, with 49 confirmed deaths, alongside 220 suspected cases and 236 suspected deaths in the DRC, though these numbers are likely an undercount.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the outbreak as a crisis exacerbated by delayed laboratory identification and regional blind spots, noting that unlike the 2013 West Africa outbreak, the DRC and its neighbours have extensive experience with viral haemorrhagic fevers.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the need for rebuilding resources, access and trust in public health systems, as containment depends on these factors given the lack of licensed vaccine or treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by delayed laboratory identification and potential undercounting of cases and deaths, though the detailed reporting of confirmed and suspected cases provides a moderate level of confidence.

analysis.summary_en: The Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring countries has been exacerbated by delayed laboratory identification and regional blind spots, leading to significant undercounting of cases and deaths. With 336 confirmed cases and 49 confirmed deaths as of 31 May, the outbreak is occurring in a region with extensive experience of viral haemorrhagic fevers but weakened by conflict and displacement. The lack of licensed vaccine or treatment means containment depends on rebuilding public health resources and trust, while the delayed response highlights the need for improved local laboratory capacity.

full_text: Ebola virus disease is often fatal and the neurological consequences in survivors are poorly characterized. A 7-year longitudinal study of 148 adult survivors of Ebola virus disease in Liberia reported headaches and altered mental status during acute infection, as well as rare cases of stroke-like symptoms or meningoencephalitis. A broad range of post-acute sequalae were identified: persistent headache (66.2%), memory loss (56.1%) and fatigue (51.1%) were among the most common. At the final evaluation, including 115 survivors and 61 close contacts (used as a control), most survivors demonstrated improvement of symptoms, but memory loss persisted in 57.4% compared with 26.2% in control individuals. The findings highlight the long-term burden of Ebola virus disease. References Original article - Billioux, B. J. Neurological manifestations in adult survivors of Ebola virus disease. analysis.research_question_and_background: Ebola virus disease is often fatal and the neurological consequences in survivors are poorly characterized.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A 7-year longitudinal study of 148 adult survivors of Ebola virus disease in Liberia was conducted, with 115 survivors and 61 close contacts included in the final evaluation as a control group.
analysis.methods: The study reported headaches and altered mental status during acute infection, as well as rare cases of stroke-like symptoms or meningoencephalitis, and evaluated a broad range of post-acute sequalae.
analysis.main_results: Persistent headache (66.2%), memory loss (56.1%) and fatigue (51.1%) were among the most common post-acute sequalae; at the final evaluation, memory loss persisted in 57.4% of survivors compared with 26.2% in control individuals.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the long-term burden of Ebola virus disease, with most survivors showing symptom improvement but persistent memory loss.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study underscores the need for long-term neurological follow-up in Ebola survivors to address persistent cognitive impairments and inform clinical management strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors, but the longitudinal design and control group provide moderate strength to the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the long-term neurological consequences of Ebola virus disease in 148 adult survivors over 7 years in Liberia. The most common post-acute sequalae included persistent headache (66.2%), memory loss (56.1%), and fatigue (51.1%). While most survivors showed symptom improvement over time, memory loss persisted in 57.4% of survivors compared to 26.2% of control individuals. The findings highlight the significant long-term burden of Ebola virus disease on neurological health, emphasizing the need for ongoing clinical follow-up and management strategies for survivors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 埃博拉病毒病 通常是致命的,并且幸存者的神经系统后果尚不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对利比里亚148名埃博拉病毒病成年幸存者进行了为期7年的纵向研究,其中115名幸存者和61名密切接触者作为对照组纳入最终评估。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究报告了急性感染期间的头痛和精神状态改变,以及罕见的中风样症状或脑膜脑炎病例,并评估了广泛的急性后后遗症。
elements_zh.main_results: 持续性头痛(66.2%)、记忆力减退(56.1%)和疲劳(51.1%)是最常见的急性后遗症;在最终评估中,57.4% 的幸存者持续丧失记忆,而对照组为 26.2%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了 埃博拉病毒病 的长期负担,大多数幸存者表现出症状改善,但记忆力持续丧失。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究强调需要对埃博拉幸存者进行长期神经学随访,以解决持续的认知障碍并为临床管理策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据受到研究的观察性质和潜在混杂因素的限制,但纵向设计和对照组为研究结果提供了中等强度。

full_text: Human brain organoids reveal how Ebola virus establishes persistent infection within the immune-privileged environment of the central nervous system. Subjects The idea of immune privilege has reshaped our understanding of how the immune system is regulated across tissues. It is viewed as a state of selective immune tolerance characterized by tissue- and organ-specific immune regulation. Classic examples include the central nervous system (CNS), eyes and testes, where immune surveillance is present but constrained. These sites maintain a highly regulated immunological milieu through cellular barriers, local immunoregulatory mediators and context-dependent modulation of antigen presentation. While this restrained inflammatory tone is essential to preserve the function and integrity of indispensable tissues, it comes at a cost: the same features that limit immunopathology can also reduce pathogen clearance. As a result, immune-privileged niches may be co-opted by pathogens as long-term reservoirs and enable persistence despite systemic immune surveillance. Understanding how viruses exploit these specialized environments is therefore critical for defining the mechanisms underlying chronic infection and relapse. Numerous studies have characterized viral replication dynamics, transmission and evolution during acute Ebola virus (EBOV) infection. However, increasing evidence indicates that EBOV can persist during the chronic phase, with ongoing viral replication in survivors supporting the concept that persistence represents an active infection within immune-privileged reservoirs1. Among these niches, the CNS has emerged as a particularly clinically relevant site, as studies in non-human primates have demonstrated that replication-competent EBOV can remain in the brain after clearance from the periphery, leading to fatal relapses2. Yet the mechanisms underlying EBOV persistence in the human CNS remain poorly understood, leaving key questions unanswered regarding the neural cell populations that support long-term infection and the associated host responses. In this issue of Nature Microbiology, Widerspick and colleagues3 provide mechanistic insights on how orthoebolaviruses exploit the CNS’s immune-privileged status to establish long-term persistence. The authors developed a human brain organoid model that enables long-term analysis of orthoebolavirus infection in the human neural tissue and tested EBOV (species Orthoebolavirus zairense), Sudan virus (species Orthoebolavirus sudanense), Reston virus (species Orthoebolavirus restonense), and a related filovirus, Marburg virus (species Orthomarburgvirus marburgense). In these organoids, they show that EBOV can persist for up to 120 days within diverse neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, microglia and oligodendrocytes. This persistence, referring to the continued presence of infectious virus or viral genetic material beyond the acute phase of infection, suggests that EBOV can establish a sustained reservoir within human neural tissue. Mechanistically, the study shows that EBOV persistence relies on both canonical viral budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission through actin-dependent cellular projections and syncytia formation. Cell-to-cell spread is recognized as a potential mechanism of immune evasion, allowing viruses to disseminate while potentially reducing exposure to soluble immune mediators4. Within highly interconnected neural tissue, this mode of spread may be advantageous, as shown by our recent work demonstrating that monkeypox virus exploits neuronal connectivity to propagate while limiting immune exposure5. Widerspick and colleagues observed that long-term persistence of EBOV was associated with ongoing viral evolution together with the accumulation of defective viral genomes. Defective viral genomes are increasingly recognized as regulators of persistent infection because they can attenuate cytopathic replication while allowing for minimal levels of viral activity. By interfering with replication of full-length viral genomes, defective viral genomes have been proposed to modulate viral replication and host responses, potentially reducing cytopathic effects and contributing to persistence6. Importantly, the study identifies marked cell type-specific differences in the host response to persistent EBOV infection. Whereas infected astrocytes remained comparatively quiescent, microglia mounted robust pro-inflammatory and type I interferon responses, identifying these cells as likely drivers of the chronic neuroinflammation associated with EBOV persistence. This observation reinforces the concept that immune privilege may support long-term viral maintenance while allowing inflammatory responses to emerge once local immune activation is engaged (Fig. 1). Similar patterns have been observed in other neurotropic viral infections. Replication-competent Zika virus, for example, can persist in the brains of surviving mice for more than 1 year within inflammatory foci enriched in activated microglia and astrocytes, where viral persistence is associated with chronic inflammation and neuronal injury7. More broadly, persistent viral reservoirs represent one of several proposed mechanisms contributing to post-acute sequelae of infection, including long COVID, in which sustained immune activation may result from a combination of viral persistence, immune dysregulation and other host factors8,9. Whether the mechanisms of CNS persistence identified for EBOV are conserved among other Orthoebolavirus species such as Bundibugyo virus — the driving pathogen of the current Ebola disease outbreak — remains unclear. Bundibugyo virus has shown evidence of CNS involvement in animal models, with viral antigen and RNA detected in CNS-associated tissues10,11, and long-term neurological sequelae reported in human survivors12. However, whether Bundibugyo virus establishes CNS persistence through similar cellular tropism and host–virus interactions remains unknown. Comparative studies will be required to determine whether CNS persistence represents a conserved feature across all orthoebolaviruses and to define the viral and host determinants that enable long-term infection within neural tissue. Although brain organoids provide a valuable platform to investigate EBOV persistence in human neural tissue, they remain a simplified representation of the CNS and do not fully recapitulate the complex immune, barrier and cellular interactions that shape viral persistence within the intact CNS. Consequently, caution is warranted when extrapolating these findings to human disease. This is particularly relevant given that the CNS maintains selective communication with the peripheral immune system through structures such as the glymphatic system and meningeal lymphatic vessels, which facilitate antigen clearance and immune cross-talk between the brain and peripheral lymphoid organs. The meninges, choroid plexus and perivascular spaces are also recognized as neuroimmune hubs that coordinate immune surveillance, antigen presentation and leukocyte trafficking13. Addressing these questions will be essential to determine whether EBOV persistence reflects escape from immune surveillance or an active adaptation to the CNS environment. Future organoid models incorporating cellular barriers, vascular components and peripheral immune cells will help determine how these virus–host interactions are shaped by neuroimmune communication and how EBOV establishes and maintains CNS reservoirs. They may also clarify whether microglia promote or restrict persistence and whether viral evolution within the CNS contributes to relapse or transmission. Collectively, these next-generation human brain models will provide a framework to investigate the mechanisms governing viral persistence in the CNS in a more physiologically relevant context. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how Ebola virus establishes persistent infection within the immune-privileged environment of the central nervous system, addressing a knowledge gap in the mechanisms underlying chronic infection and relapse.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The researchers developed a human brain organoid model to analyze orthoebolavirus infection in human neural tissue, testing Ebola virus, Sudan virus, Reston virus, and Marburg virus.
analysis.methods: The study used human brain organoids to examine viral persistence across diverse neural cell types and investigated the mechanisms of viral spread, including canonical budding and cell-to-cell transmission.
analysis.main_results: EBOV persisted for up to 120 days within neurons, astrocytes, microglia, and oligodendrocytes, relying on both viral budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission through actin-dependent projections and syncytia formation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that EBOV exploits the CNS's immune-privileged status to establish long-term persistence, with cell-to-cell spread serving as a mechanism of immune evasion.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform surveillance and treatment strategies by identifying the CNS as a potential reservoir for EBOV persistence, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to prevent relapse.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate, as the study relies on an organoid model, which may not fully replicate in vivo conditions, though the mechanistic insights provide a solid foundation for further research.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how Ebola virus (EBOV) establishes persistent infection in the central nervous system (CNS), an immune-privileged site. Using human brain organoids, the researchers demonstrated that EBOV can persist for up to 120 days in diverse neural cell types, including neurons, astrocytes, microglia, and oligodendrocytes. The persistence relies on both canonical viral budding and direct cell-to-cell transmission via actin-dependent projections and syncytia formation, which may help the virus evade immune responses. These findings provide mechanistic insights into EBOV persistence and relapse, suggesting the CNS as a potential reservoir. The study underscores the importance of targeting immune-privileged sites in surveillance and treatment strategies to prevent chronic infection and fatal relapses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解 埃博拉病毒 如何在中枢神经系统的免疫特权环境中建立持续感染,解决慢性感染和复发机制的知识空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究人员开发了一种人脑类器官模型来分析人类神经组织中的正埃博拉病毒感染,测试了埃博拉病毒、苏丹病毒、雷斯顿病毒和马尔堡病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用人脑类器官来检查病毒在不同神经细胞类型中的持久性,并研究了病毒传播的机制,包括典型出芽和细胞间 传播。
elements_zh.main_results: EBOV 在神经元、星形胶质细胞、小胶质细胞和少突胶质细胞内持续长达 120 天,依赖于病毒出芽和通过肌动蛋白依赖性投射和合胞体形成的直接细胞间 传播。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,埃博拉病毒利用中枢神经系统的免疫特权状态来建立长期持续性,细胞间传播作为免疫逃避的机制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果通过将中枢神经系统确定为埃博拉病毒持续存在的潜在 储存宿主 来为 监测 和 治疗 策略提供信息,强调需要采取有针对性的干预措施以防止复发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度中等,因为该研究依赖于类器官模型,该模型可能无法完全复制体内条件,尽管机制见解为进一步研究提供了坚实的基础。

full_text: An outbreak of Ebola disease in East-Central Africa was recently declared a public health emergency of international concern by the World Health Organization. As of June 13, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda Ministries of Health have reported 801 confirmed cases, including 178 deaths in the DRC and 2 in Uganda. Actual numbers are believed to be higher. Ebola disease is not new to the region. It was first identified in 1976 in what is now DRC and South Sudan. The virus causes a severe, often deadly illness with symptoms that include fever, diarrhea, and vomiting. Ebola disease is transmitted in humans through direct contact with blood, body fluids, or contaminated items from a symptomatic or deceased patient. Supportive care includes blood pressure maintenance, pain control, and volume repletion. The largest outbreak to date was the 2014-2016 epidemic in West Africa, when Zaire ebolavirus caused 28,600 cases and 11,000 deaths. In contrast, the current outbreak involves the Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain that has no vaccine or approved treatments. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the current risk to the U.S. population is low. Most U.S. emergency departments (EDs) are unlikely to encounter a patient with Ebola disease. Even so, experts say that emergency physicians need to be ready for low-incidence, high-consequence pathogens. The identify-isolate-inform approach is essential across all settings, from small critical access hospitals to major academic institutions. “What we want to do is be able to care for that 1 very rare, highly complex patient without disrupting the health system as a whole,” said Michael C. Wadman, MD, FACEP, professor and chair of emergency medicine at the University of Nebraska Medical Center (UNMC). He serves as medical director of the National Quarantine Unit at UNMC, a federally funded facility to monitor individuals exposed to high-consequence infectious diseases. Since the outbreak of Bundibugyo virus began, Dr Wadman has heard from many emergency medicine colleagues seeking information on how to prepare for a potential case. “Knowing up front that it's out there and knowing that you're potentially going to be encountering travelers with exposure risk, is the key,” he said. What's Different About Bundibugyo Virus Several factors have made this outbreak hard to detect and control. Angela Hewlett, MD, MS, is professor of infectious diseases at UNMC and medical director of the Nebraska Biocontainment Unit, one of 13 Regional Emerging Special Pathogen Treatment Centers, or RESPTCs, in the United States. This is only the third known outbreak to involve Bundibugyo virus, Dr Hewlett explained. The unusual strain went undetected for several weeks, partly because frontline diagnostic tests are designed for the Zaire species. The first suspected case was a health care worker who developed symptoms on April 24, 2026; laboratory confirmation was received 21 days later. Other obstacles include incomplete contact tracing, security incidents, and a lack of treatment options (although products are in development). “The strain doesn't have any approved therapeutics, as opposed to Zaire ebolavirus, for which we have two FDA-approved therapeutic agents and an effective vaccine,” said Dr Hewlett. “It's a difficult scenario right now in Africa, and one that I think we should all be paying attention to.” Clinically, Ebola disease presents with nonspecific early symptoms that can overlap with other infectious diseases, such as malaria and typhoid fever. In the ED, rapid identification is critical to safely care for these patients and preserve health system function. What EDs Can Do Now Preparedness begins at the front desk, Dr Hewlett and Dr Wadman emphasized. As a first step in the identify-isolate-inform framework, they recommend that EDs conduct symptom and travel screening for all patients. At UNMC, EHR modules are leveraged for this purpose. “We ask every patient if they have fever, cough, or rash and whether they've traveled internationally in the last month. If yes, we immediately put a mask on the patient and ask where they traveled,” said Dr Hewlett. “Our EHR fires an alert if that's one of the concerning outbreak zones.” From there, the alert can guide staff through next steps, including moving the patient to a private room, selecting appropriate PPE, and handling lab draws. Chains of communication are another challenge, Dr Hewlett noted. “The ‘inform’ piece not only involves your internal communications but also external communications. Once you get the patient identified and isolated, typically the first call would be to the local public health authority.” As a best practice, EDs should have a written plan with up-to-date phone numbers that is rapidly accessible to all employees. Dr Wadman added that patients with low-incidence, high-consequence pathogens such as Bundibugyo virus do sometimes make it past triage to the inpatient environment. “Their pathway through that hospital can expose a lot of people to that infection. It brings us right back to identifying these folks up front,” he said. Preparedness Is Partnership At UNMC, training exercises and walkthroughs are another key component. “Secret shopper” drills in the ED, as well as more complex scenarios (eg, patient transfer to the operating room, simulations in full PPE), help ensure that patients with high-consequence pathogens still receive appropriate care. Dr Hewlett and Dr Wadman also stressed the critical importance of coordinating with local EMS agencies, fire departments, and transport services. Patients with suspected or confirmed high-consequence pathogens may need transfer from their home to a medical facility or from a smaller facility to a higher-level center. Emergency transportation partners should be included in drills and training. Bundibugyo virus is unlikely to reach most U.S. EDs, but preparedness remains a team effort. “It's really a partnership,” said Dr Hewlett. “The ED teams are on the front lines and are the ones who will identify, isolate, and inform early on.” “Emergency medicine and infectious disease are an outstanding combination for dealing with these sorts of high-consequence, complex cases,” Dr Wadman agreed. “You'll have a well-coordinated response with people who can provide expert patient care.” How to Prepare for Potential Ebola Exposures - Ask every patient about cough, fever, rash, and recent international travel. - Use EHR modules to flag travel from affected countries and guide next steps. - Designate separate spaces for patients, donning/doffing procedures, and waste management. - Create an accessible action plan. - Know who to call (eg, infection prevention, medical directors, public health). - Practice the process (eg, “secret shopper” drills). - Include emergency medical services (EMS) and transport teams in planning and training.
